clue.text: Shoe sent back to headquarters, with end bit missing

indicators.note: sent back tells us the whole string built here is read in the opposite direction
the final letter of the word for headquarters is dropped, its end bit gone

parts.note: a base is a headquarters, as in an army base

explanation.surface: A shoe has been returned to head office with a piece broken off its end.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sent back' turns the whole run TOBAS around; 'with end bit missing' drops the final E of the headquarters word. A sabot is a clog, which gave us the word sabotage.
explanation.definitionFit: A sabot is a wooden clog, the traditional peasant footwear of France and the Low Countries.

clue.text: Footballer — one place to watch him away?

parts.note: a stand is a place for spectators to watch a match
off means away, as in going off

explanation.surface: Where can fans see a player when he plays away from home?
explanation.walkthrough: In rugby football the stand-off (fly-half) is the back who links scrum-half and threequarters; 'Footballer' hides that rugby sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The stand-off half is a rugby player in the key playmaking position behind the scrum.

clue.text: Wipe up, looking very angry after break-in

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: to rub is to wipe a surface
glary means glaring, looking fiercely angry

explanation.surface: Someone is cleaning up, furious after a robbery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wipe up' looks like a phrase about cleaning, but 'up' turns RUB in this down clue to give BUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Burglary is the crime of breaking into a building to steal.

clue.text: Quiz score?

parts.note: a score is twenty, and a quiz consists of questions, so a score of quiz items describes a parlour game

explanation.walkthrough: 'Score' reads as the points total in a quiz, but here it is the old word for twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: The parlour game has players identify a thing by asking up to a score of yes-or-no queries.

clue.text: Low-budget version of Hotel is failure with audience

parts.note: a flop is a failure, like a show that closes early
the house is the audience in a theatre, as in a full house

explanation.surface: A cut-price hotel turns out a disaster with the guests.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a long descriptive phrase: a cheap, shabby lodging house.
explanation.definitionFit: A flophouse is a very cheap, run-down lodging, the bottom end of the hotel trade.

clue.text: Travelled by plane, making audible complaint

indicators.note: audible means a word heard aloud stands in for the one entered

parts.note: flu is a complaint, an illness

explanation.surface: A passenger grumbles loudly on a flight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Complaint' suggests grumbling, but it is an illness, the flu.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who went somewhere on an aircraft did so by air.

clue.text: Thus soup might be made unavailable?

definitions.meaning: soup is made by starting from a stock of bones and vegetables
unavailable means sold out, none left in the shop

explanation.surface: A shortage of ingredients means the soup cannot be served.
explanation.definitionFit: Soup is made from stock, while goods sold out in a shop have none left on the shelves.

clue.text: Under new arrangement, I lease old French university accommodation

indicators.note: under a new arrangement means the letters that follow are reordered

explanation.surface: Someone rents out an old French property to students on fresh terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The fifteen letters of I LEASE OLD FRENCH are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A hall of residence is a building where students at a university live.

clue.text: University trained nurse lacking in self-confidence

indicators.note: trained means shaped or worked into a new form, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A university-trained nurse has little faith in herself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trained' sounds like the nurse's qualification, but it is the signal to rework the letters of the nurse word into NSURE, placed after U.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unsure means doubting oneself, lacking confidence.

clue.text: Book time in Surrey location

indicators.note: in means the abbreviation for time is placed inside the Surrey town

parts.note: Esher is a town in Surrey, south-west of London

explanation.surface: Someone books a time slot at a place in Surrey.
explanation.walkthrough: Surrey is a county just south-west of London; 'Book' is a book of the Bible, not a reservation.
explanation.definitionFit: Esther is a book of the Old Testament, telling the story of the Jewish queen of Persia.

clue.text: People enter into a welcome understanding

indicators.note: the people are placed inside the word for welcome, as if entering it

parts.note: to greet is to welcome
men is a common crossword word for people

explanation.surface: Folk step into a friendly greeting that seals a deal.
explanation.definitionFit: An agreement is a mutual understanding or accord between parties.

clue.text: Collection of names includes unknown composer

indicators.note: includes means the unknown letter sits inside the word for a collection of names

parts.note: a list is a collection of names, such as a guest list
in algebra x, y and z stand for unknowns, so Z is an unknown

explanation.surface: A register of names contains a composer nobody has heard of.
explanation.walkthrough: Mathematicians use x, y and z for unknown quantities, a convention crosswords borrow freely.
explanation.definitionFit: Franz Liszt was a Hungarian Romantic composer and piano virtuoso.

clue.text: Speak at length using elaborate detail

indicators.note: elaborate as a verb means work up or rework, signalling the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone talks at great length, going into elaborate detail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Elaborate' looks like a description of the detail, but it reworks the six letters of DETAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: To dilate on a subject is to discourse about it expansively, at great length.

clue.text: Mostly away from the beaten track? Definitely

indicators.note: mostly means the phrase is not used in full; one letter is dropped from it

parts.note: off course means away from the planned route, off the beaten track

explanation.surface: Someone asked whether they are lost far from the usual path replies emphatically yes.
explanation.walkthrough: OFF COURSE loses one of its two Fs under 'Mostly'.
explanation.definitionFit: Said in reply, the phrase is an emphatic yes, meaning certainly or naturally.

clue.text: Reserve keeper warned off after match

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters come below the word for match in this down entry

parts.note: a game is a match, a sporting contest

indicators.note: off means the letters of warned are spoiled, put in a different order

explanation.surface: A substitute goalkeeper is cautioned once the match is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Reserve keeper' reads like a sporting substitute, but it is someone who guards a nature reserve. 'Off' turns WARNED into WARDEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A game warden protects wildlife in a reserve or park and enforces hunting laws.

clue.text: Parts of a horse, or the whole lot, one might say

indicators.note: one might say signals a word spoken that sounds the same as the one entered

parts.note: four quarters make a whole, so four quarters is the whole lot

explanation.surface: Part of a horse, or perhaps all of it, as someone might put it.
explanation.walkthrough: Four quarters make up the whole of anything, and said out loud the phrase matches the horse's front sections.
explanation.definitionFit: A horse's front body, legs and shoulders together are called its forehand or front quarters.

clue.text: Halt transfer

definitions.meaning: to stop doing something, as in a plea to quit nagging
to hand something across to another person

explanation.definitionFit: Stopping an annoying behaviour or handing over possession are both senses of the phrasal verb.

clue.text: Spent too little time in bed, it may be felt?

definitions.text: Spent too little time in bed
definitions.meaning: lying down for less time than needed, a playful under-sleep
the layer laid beneath carpet, which is often made of felt

explanation.surface: Someone short of sleep can feel it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Felt' looks like the past of feel, but it is the fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words, lay too little; as one word, the padding beneath a carpet, often made of felt fabric.

clue.text: Indirect effect concerning group taking a beating?

parts.note: re means concerning or about, as in business letters
the percussion section of an orchestra is the group whose instruments are beaten

explanation.surface: A band gets thrashed, with knock-on consequences.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'beating' is drumming, not punishment: the percussion section strikes its instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: A repercussion is a consequence that follows on indirectly from an action.

clue.text: Pick up excellent engagements out east in major venues

indicators.note: in a down clue pick up means the letters are raised, read from the bottom upward

parts.note: A1 means excellent, written here as the letters AI

indicators.note: east, E, is taken out of the word for engagements

parts.note: dates are engagements or appointments

explanation.surface: Collect top-quality bookings, leaving the east, in big arenas.
explanation.walkthrough: AI plus DATS (DATES with E removed, 'out east') makes AIDATS, which 'Pick up' reverses in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Stadia is a plural of stadium, a large sports or concert arena.

clue.text: Carpenter seen in fast-food outlet

definitions.meaning: a woodworker, called a ... in British slang

explanation.surface: A joiner is spotted in a takeaway.
explanation.walkthrough: Both senses are British slang: a woodworker, and a shop selling fish and chips.
explanation.definitionFit: British informal speech uses one word for both a joiner and a fish-and-chip shop.

clue.text: Islander's expression of surprise captured by painter

indicators.note: captured by means the exclamation is held inside the painter's name

parts.note: Titian was a Venetian Renaissance painter
ah is an exclamation of surprise

explanation.surface: A painter catches the gasp of someone from a South Pacific island.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Islander's' reads as 'Islander is', with the 's as a link. Gauguin is the painter linked with the island, but Titian supplies the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tahitian is a native of Tahiti, an island in French Polynesia.

clue.text: Notice woman's taking end of orange stick

parts.note: an ad is a notice, short for advertisement
her is the woman's, a possessive pronoun

indicators.note: end of picks out only the last letter of the word orange

explanation.surface: A poster shows a woman holding the tip of an orange stick.
explanation.walkthrough: An orange stick is a manicure tool, which makes 'stick' look like part of the picture rather than a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To adhere is to stick fast to a surface.

clue.text: Heroine's shown up by end of programme

indicators.note: shown up in a down clue means the letters are displayed reading upward, backwards
end of means the last few letters of the word programme are taken

explanation.surface: The leading lady appears in the final scene of a show.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition 'Heroine's' reads as 'Heroine is'. The last four letters of 'programme' are read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma Woodhouse is the title heroine of Jane Austen's novel.

clue.text: Habitual drinker goes bathing with nothing on

parts.note: to dip is to go for a quick swim
O looks like zero, so it stands for nothing

explanation.surface: A heavy drinker goes skinny-dipping.
explanation.definitionFit: Dipso is slang short for dipsomaniac, an alcoholic.

clue.text: Evil demon's new appearance in melodramatic story

indicators.note: a new appearance means the letters take on a fresh order

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written

explanation.surface: A wicked fiend reappears in a sensational tale.
explanation.walkthrough: The nine letters of EVIL DEMON are rearranged under 'new appearance'.
explanation.definitionFit: A dime novel was a cheap, sensational paperback adventure, sold originally for ten cents.

clue.text: Deep gorge in island to the west of a former African state

indicators.note: in an across answer to the west of means placed to the left, so before the final letter

parts.note: an abyss is a deep chasm or gorge

explanation.surface: A ravine lies on an island, west of somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: Abyssinia is the old name for Ethiopia, the empire in the Horn of Africa.

clue.text: Evidently, class is leaving in good time

indicators.note: is leaving means the abbreviation for class goes out of the larger word

parts.note: clearly means evidently, obviously
cl is an abbreviation for class

explanation.surface: Plainly the class is going home ahead of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Early means before the expected time, ahead of schedule.
